title: Phase 1b: the window must stop counting turns for itself
description:
Client half of the ledger (pcg-b2z). render.js state.inflight counts user_echo and decrements on result, which is the same wrong pairing as the server's counter -- it is what leaves the pulse breathing forever after a fold.

Shape, once the server mints a uuid per send (pcg-b2z) and echoes it on wrapper/user_echo:
- state.inflight (int) -> state.outstanding (Set of command_uuid). Also in newRenderScope() at render.js:646, so every background tab keeps its own.
- wrapper/user_echo carries the uuid -> add it. 'queued' (keep the existing pulse rather than starting a new one) becomes simply !!state.pulse, which is what that test always meant.
- new case: command_lifecycle. A terminal state (completed/cancelled/discarded/refused) deletes the uuid; when the set empties, settlePulse() + resetTurn() + busy false. Ignore states for uuids we never sent (the CLI mints its own for cron triggers and teammate prompts).
- result: stop settling on it. resetTurn(state.outstanding.size > 0). For a fresh turn 'completed' lands microseconds after the result (measured), so there is no visible delay.
- wrapper/idle_sync and cli_exited: clear the set, unchanged otherwise -- they stay the backstop.

MIND THE FREE GATE: spec-test.html:1034 fires a bare result and then asserts the pulse settled into its closing line (and :1045 that it moved to the end). After this change a result alone no longer settles, so that case must emit the matching command_lifecycle/completed -- which is what the real server does. Do NOT weaken the assertion instead; it is the only guard on the closing line.
notes: REGRESSION GUARD (added at review, 2026-08-24): keep the aborted_streaming special case. Today render.js:1514 zeroes the count instantly when result.terminal_reason === 'aborted_streaming'; nothing else reaches the client instantly on interrupt (the wrapper publishes no interrupt event the renderer consumes -- checked render.js:1660-1734). If phase 1b drops ALL result-based settling before phase 2 lands the interrupt receipt, every Stop leaves the pulse breathing ~5s until wrapper/idle_sync. So: on result with terminal_reason === 'aborted_streaming', clear state.outstanding entirely (a no-op if a terminal lifecycle already emptied it). Phase 2 may later refine this with the receipt's cancelled[]/still_queued[], but the clear is harmless to keep.
close_reason: Done 2026-08-24: state.inflight -> state.outstanding Set (newRenderScope too), user_echo carries the uuid, command_lifecycle terminal states delete it, empty set settles the pulse. result no longer settles except aborted_streaming clears the set (regression guard kept per review note). idle_sync/cli_exited/resumed/reset clear. spec-test.html cases updated to emit lifecycle, not weakened -- gate grew 150->153 and the new cases negative-test the old counter by construction.

title: Phase 1: replace the send-counter with a uuid ledger
description:
Root cause of the stuck spinner, server half. MEASURED 2026-08-24 by probe_queue.py (PASS 8/8, free) -- no guesswork left except the fold's own ordering, which needs a paid turn.

WHAT THE CLI DOES (wiki/cli-stream-json-findings.md):
  send  {"type":"user","uuid":"<uuid4>","message":{...}}     <- uuid at the TOP LEVEL, not inside message
  recv  command_lifecycle queued / started ... result ... command_lifecycle completed
A fresh turn emits completed AFTER its result; a folded one emits it BEFORE. Either way the set
empties at the right instant, which is the whole point of using it instead of counting results.

CHANGES in server.py ClaudeSession:
- _inflight (int) -> _outstanding (set of uuid strings). busy = bool(_outstanding). _reset_inflight -> clears the set and _recap_wanted as it does today.
- send_blocks(): mint uuid.uuid4(), add it under the existing lock BEFORE _write_line (same reason the increment is there today -- a fast result must not beat the bookkeeping), put it on the frame, and return it so /api/message can echo it on wrapper/user_echo for the window (pcg-ygk).
- reader loop: on command_lifecycle, discard command_uuid from the set when state is terminal (completed/cancelled/discarded/refused). Ignore uuids we never sent -- the CLI mints its own for cron triggers, teammate prompts and deferred-turn resume, and those emit started/terminal with no queued.
- result no longer decrements anything. _after_result keeps the title/usage/statusline work.

BACKSTOP, required not optional -- the schema documents holes the ledger cannot see: a turn that
fails by throwing leaves 'started' with no terminal state, and an older CLI emits nothing at all.
Arm the existing silence watchdog on every result (_idle_deadline = now + IDLE_SYNC_SECONDS,
_arm_idle_sync), disarm it in send_blocks, and have _sync_idle clear the set and publish idle_sync
instead of returning early on a non-empty count. Safe precisely because it is armed only after a
result: a turn that really is queued starts talking within milliseconds and _touch_idle pushes the
deadline out, while a CLI with nothing left to do says nothing. Today _idle_deadline is only ever
set inside interrupt(), so the watchdog cannot fire on a normal turn at all.

Also per the CLI's own instruction: on process exit, synthesize 'discarded' for uuids that never
reached a terminal state.

DO NOT gate any of this on the capability list: capabilities lives on system/init, not on the
initialize reply, and system/init is not emitted until the first turn starts. The watchdog is the
version-independent fallback.
close_reason: Done 2026-08-24: _inflight -> _outstanding uuid ledger (lock-guarded, uuid top-level on the frame, terminal lifecycle discards, unknown uuids ignored). Silence watchdog armed on every result in the reader (recap's swallowed result included), disarmed in send_blocks, _sync_idle clears the set. Synthetic 'discarded' on process exit. BONUS beyond spec: _lifecycle_seen compat -- pre-2.1.241 CLIs get one synthetic 'completed' per result, so old counter semantics survive on one code path (unchanged test_units.py proves it). Gates: spec 153/153, units PASS, transcript guard PASS.

title: Phase 0: free probe of command_lifecycle and the capability list
description:
No paid turn. Spawn the real CLI with our exact CLAUDE_ARGS and measure:

- system/init (and the initialize reply) actually advertise msg_lifecycle_v1, interrupt_receipt_v1, interrupt_cancel_queued_v1 on THIS build.
- A user frame carrying a top-level lowercase-uuid 'uuid' produces command_lifecycle events on stdout. Payload: /recap on an empty session -- documented to refuse FOR FREE (CLAUDE.md), so the whole round trip costs no tokens.
- The exact state sequence and its ordering relative to result.
- Control: the same frame WITHOUT a uuid emits no lifecycle events.
- cancel_async_message against a uuid that was never enqueued -> {cancelled:false} (free no-op).

The uuid must match ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-... (the CLI validates it; uuid.uuid4() qualifies). The one thing this probe exists to pin is the FIELD PLACEMENT on the inbound frame -- top-level uuid vs somewhere else -- which is assumption today, not measurement.

Exit: the answers written into wiki/cli-stream-json-findings.md, version-pinned to 2.1.241.

Headlines: the uuid goes at the TOP LEVEL of the user frame (not inside message); queued->started->completed with completed AFTER the result for a fresh turn; no uuid means no lifecycle events at all; cancel_async_message answers {cancelled:false} free. AND: capabilities is NOT on the initialize reply -- it is on system/init, which is not emitted until the first turn starts, so nothing can gate on it at spawn.

title: Mirror the CLI's message-queue contract (fold, lifecycle, cancel)
description:
The window's busy state is derived from a send-counter that assumes one result per send. CLI 2.1.241 broke that assumption and offers an exact replacement we do not use.

MEASURED against the 2.1.241 bundle + the D--Project transcript e9ecc3c6:
1. A mid-turn send is FOLDED into the running turn, not queued as its own turn. Transcript shows queue-operation:enqueue -> attachment:queued_command -> queue-operation:remove, and the CLI's own comment reads 'it never runs as its own turn'. Several queued prompts also MERGE into one turn at turn start.
   => N sends can produce ONE result. _inflight and state.inflight leak upward forever. This is the reported 'it still says it is thinking'.
2. command_lifecycle is a real stdout event in -p/SDK sessions:
   {type:'command_lifecycle', command_uuid, state:'queued|started|completed|cancelled|discarded|refused', uuid, session_id}
   command_uuid is the CLIENT-SUPPLIED uuid on the inbound message. 'Commands enqueued without a uuid emit no lifecycle events.' We never send a uuid, so the channel is off.
   Ordering: a command that starts a fresh turn emits completed AFTER that turn's result; a folded command emits completed BEFORE it.
   Documented holes: a turn that throws can leave 'started' with no terminal state; a dropped message can leave 'queued' with no terminal; wrapper should synthesize 'discarded' on process exit.
3. interrupt does NOT cancel queued commands by default. cancel_queued:true is required; the response carries cancelled[] and still_queued[].
4. cancel_async_message {message_uuid} -> {cancelled:bool} drops one pending message.
5. system/init advertises capabilities: msg_lifecycle_v1, interrupt_receipt_v1, interrupt_cancel_queued_v1.

Children cover the probe, the ledger, stop-means-stop, the queue UI, and the replay data-loss.

title: Context meter briefly reads 100% mid-session - the result-event estimate is wrong arithmetic
description:
Reported: the context notice flashes 'full, compact now' and corrects itself a moment later.

Not a string match this time (that flicker was fixed in the 2026-08-18 pass). Two figures feed the same number and the WRONG one is faster.

render.js:1481-1490, on every result event:
    const window_ = ev.modelUsage ? Object.values(ev.modelUsage)[0]?.contextWindow : undefined;
    const used = usage.input_tokens + usage.cache_read_input_tokens + usage.cache_creation_input_tokens;
    setStatus({ context: Math.round(used / window_ * 100) })

Measured against the 2.1.241 schema:
- modelUsage is a MAP KEYED BY MODEL, and its own doc reads: 'Per-model totals for every model call made through the query pipeline -- main loop, Task subagents, sidechains, and internal calls such as compaction and Workflow agents. Cumulative across turns in streaming-input sessions.'
  So Object.values(...)[0] is an ARBITRARY model -- whichever key was inserted first. On a session running claude-fable-5[1m] (1M window) that has ever touched a 200k-class model (a subagent, a compaction call, an internal helper), the denominator is 200k while the numerator is the aggregate across all of them.
  Real numbers from the reported session (transcript e9ecc3c6): cache_read 282381 tokens. True load ~28% of 1M. Divided by a 200k window: 141%.
- ev.usage is the aggregate over all those calls, so numerator and denominator are not even about the same model.
- meter() clamps with Math.min(100, pct), which is why the user sees exactly 100% -- the clamp is the tell that the computed value was >= 100. noteContext gets the RAW value and fires the notice at WARN_AT=85.

Why it self-corrects: _publish_usage asks get_context_usage, whose answer IS authoritative ('Rounded total_tokens / raw_max_tokens') and overwrites it -- but that call takes 13-60s on this PC (CONTEXT_USAGE_TIMEOUT=60, wiki/control-protocol.md section 9). The estimate lands instantly, the truth lands up to a minute later. Every turn. That is the whole flicker.

FIX (mirrors the CLI, and deletes code): the CLI's own meter comes from get_context_usage and nothing else. Drop the result-event estimate. setStatus merges, so the meter simply keeps its last real value between turns instead of being repainted with a wrong one.

If the estimate is kept for the first-paint gap instead, it must (a) key on state.status.model, which system/init already sets (render.js:1232), not on Object.values()[0], and (b) never reach noteContext -- an estimate may move a meter, it may not raise a nag.

Gate: run_spec_test.py drives renderEvent directly, so a case with modelUsage carrying two models (one 200k, one 1M) and the session on the 1M one asserts the notice stays hidden.
close_reason: Done 2026-08-24: the result-event context estimate deleted (Object.values(modelUsage)[0] arithmetic and the context: key); the meter now keeps its last authoritative wrapper/usage value between turns, exactly the CLI's own source. Negative-tested: old code FAIL 154/156 (notice fired at 141%, meter clamped to 100), fixed code PASS 156/156. render.js result case no longer references modelUsage/contextWindow at all.

title: Phase 4: a folded mid-turn message vanishes from history on refresh
description:
CONFIRMED on the real transcript (D--Project e9ecc3c6, line 521): a message sent mid-turn is written ONLY as {type:'attachment', attachment:{type:'queued_command', prompt:[...]}}. There is no type:'user' record for it anywhere in the file.

read_session() keeps only user/assistant lines ('everything else ... is bookkeeping and would only add noise'), and _normalize_transcript_event returns None for an attachment. So: send a message while a turn is running, refresh the window, and your own message is gone from the transcript -- while the answer to it is still there.

Fix at the normalizer, which is the one choke point both replay callers route through: map attachment/queued_command to a user message carrying attachment.prompt. commandMode must be 'prompt' and isMeta must be absent -- task-notification and meta folds are the CLI's own traffic and stay filtered.

Gate: test_units.py replays a fixture containing one queued_command attachment and asserts the prompt text comes back as a user event.

Unit fixture from the measured e9ecc3c6 shape: 2 of 4 lines replay, folded Persian prompt verbatim. Gates: units PASS (3/3 new), spec 153/153, transcript guard PASS.

title: Phase 2: stop must actually stop - interrupt needs cancel_queued and its receipt read
description:
Measured: 'queued commands survive the interrupt and are listed under still_queued... A Stop-means-stop-everything client sets this true so one round-trip halts the session; older CLIs ignore the field and behave as if false.'

We send a bare interrupt with wait=False and then call _reset_inflight() on the assumption that the CLI cancelled the queue. It does not. So after stop, a queued message can still run -- while the window has already settled the pulse and hidden the stop button. The answer then arrives with no spinner and no way out.

- Send interrupt with cancel_queued:true UNCONDITIONALLY (this window IS a stop-means-stop client). Do NOT try to gate on the interrupt_cancel_queued_v1 capability: capabilities lives on system/init, which is not emitted until the first turn starts, so nothing can gate at spawn (measured 2026-08-24, probe_queue.py). Older CLIs 'ignore the field and behave as if false' -- exactly today's behaviour, so the fallback is free.
- READ the interrupt response and publish the receipt's cancelled[] and still_queued[] so the ledger settles on fact instead of assumption: discard every uuid in cancelled[] from _outstanding; leave still_queued[] in place.
- Mind wiki/control-protocol.md section 9 before giving this read a timeout -- post-result control requests on this PC can take 13-60s; the interrupt request itself is answered fast, but do not share a timeout with get_context_usage.

Note the docs' warning for resenders: 'cancelled' also arrives for user-requested removals, so correlate against our own cancel_async_message responses and the interrupt receipt before treating it as a failure.
notes: Measured 2026-08-24: interrupt_cancel_queued_v1 IS advertised on this build, but capabilities lives on system/init and system/init is not emitted until the first turn starts -- so the flag cannot be gated at spawn. Send cancel_queued:true unconditionally; older CLIs 'ignore the field and behave as if false', which is exactly today's behaviour, so the fallback is free.
close_reason: Done 2026-08-24: interrupt sends cancel_queued:true unconditionally (write stays on the caller's thread so a dead process still 409s), receipt awaited off-thread with its own 5s INTERRUPT_RECEIPT_TIMEOUT: cancelled[] uuids leave the ledger with a synthetic command_lifecycle/cancelled published, still_queued[] deliberately stays. No receipt / non-success -> quiet-window fallback, silence-window unit section untouched verbatim. control() split into _send_control/_await_control, byte-identical for existing callers. Negative-tested (4 new assertions fail on old code). Gates: units PASS (11 new OK), spec 156/156, transcript guard PASS. Follow-ups routed to pcg-suh: two stale wiki lines (parity-chrome idle_sync, findings line ~316), dead _interrupt_seq, probe_queue.py does not drive an interrupt.

title: statusline: custom statusLine command never runs (cmd.exe quote stripping)

title: Phase 3: show the queue - a message sent mid-turn is queued, not sent
description:
Parity gap, and the reason the reported bug was invisible to us. The CLI keeps a visible command queue you can cancel; our window draws a mid-turn send as an ordinary user bubble, so it LOOKS delivered while it is actually sitting in a queue that may be folded, merged, or dropped.

- On send while busy: render the text in a queued strip above the composer (dim, «در صف»), not as a transcript bubble.
- On lifecycle 'started': it becomes a real user bubble in the transcript, which is also where the CLI puts it.
- On 'cancelled'/'discarded'/'refused': the strip entry says so and the text goes back into the composer rather than being lost.
- Per-item cancel -> control cancel_async_message {message_uuid}; response {cancelled:bool} decides whether the row disappears or stays (it is a no-op once the message has been dequeued for execution).

Depends on the ledger (uuids) from Phase 1. Design restraint per the project's UI direction: one dim row per queued message, no animation, no counter chrome.

Per-row cancel: POST /api/queue/cancel -> cancel_async_message, row settles on the CLI's own {cancelled:bool} AND the synthetic lifecycle event through one idempotent dropQueued(). value: AskUserQuestion is NOT a separate channel on claude 2.1.223: it arrives as an ordinary inbound can_use_tool control_request with tool_name='AskUserQuestion' and input.questions. The ANSWER rides back in the allow reply's updatedInput.answers, keyed by the QUESTION TEXT (not index, not header); value is an option label string, an array of labels, or a ', '-joined string for multiSelect; free text is accepted. Allowing with the input unchanged answers nothing -> 'The user did not answer the questions.' Three guards required: exclude it from auto-approve AND remembered-allow (the posture would eat the question), give it its own timeout (the CLI's askUserQuestionTimeout defaults to 'never', so PERMISSION_TIMEOUT was the only thing killing it), and on timeout ALLOW with no answers (the CLI's own Skip) rather than deny, which reaches the model as a tool error. PowerShell 5.1 + $ErrorActionPreference='Stop': a native command's stderr becomes a TERMINATING NativeCommandError, so '& $exe args 2>&1 | ForEach-Object {...}' aborts the whole script on the first stderr line. Separately: Invoke-Expression runs text in the CALLER's scope - an 'exit 1' inside it terminates the calling script WITHOUT running the surrounding catch, and a 'Set-StrictMode -Version Latest' inside it governs every later line of the caller. claude.ai/install.ps1 does both, so run vendor installers as a child powershell process. A reviewer subagent running 'git checkout -- <path>' to undo its own negative-test edit reverts the file to HEAD, discarding ALL uncommitted work in it from other tasks. Happened TWICE on 2026-09-08: static/js/controls.js (MA4-T2 review, recovered from the agent's own /tmp backup) and static-terminal/index.html (TP1 review, recovered from C:\Users\Lion\AppData\Local\Temp\idx_backup.html). Both agents had made a backup first, which is the only reason nothing was lost. reviewer.md line 16 already said 'never modify git state'; both rationalized it as restoring, not modifying. Fixed 2026-09-08 by naming the exact commands in ~/.claude/agents/reviewer.md and telling reviewers to revert a negative test byte-for-byte with a checksum, or report the assertion unverified. Detection: git diff --stat on the file shows empty (identical to HEAD) when it should show the task's changes.

Transcript 'user' message.content has TWO shapes: the wrapper's own stream-json turns replay as [{type:'text'}], but a session started in the interactive CLI stores the typed prompt as a bare STRING. Array-only code fails silently in both directions (no sidebar preview; renderEvent iterating a string char-by-char renders zero user bubbles). That string is also often NOT a prompt - the CLI injects <local-command-caveat>, <command-name>, <system-reminder> envelopes as user turns. Handled once in server.py user_prompt_text(), used by session_meta() and read_session(); read_session normalises to the block shape and drops envelopes (regex ^\s*<[a-z][a-z-]+>) so the client sees one shape. Measured 2026-08-05 on claude 2.1.222.
